newsitem.title: USA: Enron, Ore. unable to agree on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Enron, Ore. unable to agree on rate cut.

text.p: The staff of the Oregon Public Utility Commission (OPUC), Enron Corp, and Portland General Electric Co were unable to agree on a rate cut for the Portland utility's customers, sources close to the talks said Wednesday.

The sides met in Salem, Ore., Wednesday morning to negotiate terms for the companies' planned merger. An acceptable rate cut to Portland General customers is a major requirement for winning regulatory approval for the deal.
The talks are currently adjourned but expected to reconvene at about 1330 PST/1630 EST/2130 GMT.
Oregon Public Utility Commission spokesman Mike Allegre said the commission is "not hopeful" of reaching agreement with the companies, which have raised their rate cut offer to $61 million.
The commission staff is asking for a rate reduction of $105 million before it will approve the $2.1-billion stock-for-stock merger.

Neither side has so far indicated over how long a period their latest proposed rate cuts would apply, though initial proposals indicated customers would see lower utility bills over a four-year period.
The commission staff had originally sought a rate cut of $189.6 million for Portland General customers over four years.
But Enron officials said the companies may ask for a hearing of the case, since the commission staff "is still far apart on facts," Allegre said.
The commission, however, "is not going to come down further. It is time to fish or cut bait," he added.
This afternoon's session will likely result in formalization of a tentative schedule for further commission action on the merger filing, the spokesman said.
That will likely include an early April target for a proposed order from the OPUC staff with written comments due at the end of April.
Oral arguments in the case would be heard in early May with June 4 set as the tentative deadline for a final decision by the commission.
The OPUC had previously set March 17 as the target for a final decision, but protracted negotiations over the rate cut issue made that impossible.
